quote: a crystal willow, a poplar of water, / a tall fountain the wind arches over, / a tree deep-rooted yet dancing still, / a course of a river that turns, moves on, / doubles back, and comes full circle, / forever arriving.
source: Octavio Paz, Sunstone, the closing six lines (trans. Eliot Weinberger, 1987)

evidence.where: archive.org full text of a 2004 Burning Man Books (Scriptor Press) printing of Sunstone in the Weinberger text, which prints the opening and the closing six lines with this wording and lineation; the same six lines, same lineation, quoted in José Quiroga's criticism on Encyclopedia.com, whose sources list the Weinberger Collected Poems, New Directions, pp. 3 to 35. The New Directions page itself was not seen
evidence.edition: Eliot Weinberger, The Collected Poems of Octavio Paz 1957 to 1987, New Directions, 1987
evidence.locator: the last six lines, repeating the first six; the poem ends on a colon, closed here to a full stop

reason: Wording and six line lineation read in a printed reprint of the Weinberger text and in published criticism, both ending on forever arriving with a colon; the closing lines repeat the opening exactly, preceded by the sun's magic of mirrors revived. Medium only because the New Directions page was not seen.
